answer.answer: Audit-ready takeover complete. The import is preserved and verified, but remains a legacy audit package rather than a second canonical game-data snapshot. Its `23761620` claim is corrected to the latest observed public executable, while canonical numeric data remains pinned to the existing two-axis snapshot. Duplicate structured data was not promoted; only distinct player context and explicitly qualified overrides or assumptions were promoted. The rejected Flowworks study remains historical evidence and cannot override the July 11 staged plan.

claims.value: `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip`, supplied on 2026-07-11, was imported losslessly as `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z`. The original archive is exactly 21,674,717 bytes with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`; it contains 123 entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. `unzip -t` passed and every packaged SHA-256 passed. The import ledger records `imported_at` `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`, archive retrieval time `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`, and integrity status `verified`. The unchanged ZIP and verified extracted tree are retained under `imports/star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z/raw`, intentionally ignored by Git because they duplicate third-party data, personalized context, generated binaries, and a legacy SQLite database; tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` retain the audit inventory. Preserved legacy hashes include SQLite `d9ffbae20414d9e05a5dc02a664c904bc2bf0b8d74c8ae427ee9e8dccf6669fc`, snapshot JSON `373e0f0dc556ce9cc03120321356bf7ce85fc012ffd7b49ce1aac3e89e6abf59`, and workbook `2cb9f89360b9a721b2f41771ac77643a0438cb27e96b4f84a161ba93e7e04263`.

The archive’s repeated attribution of numeric data to Steam build `23761620` is not reliable provenance: its source-site version and numeric game-build identity were not recorded reliably. Two independent axes must be retained. On the game-data axis, the canonical source claims Update 1 internal version `35118973`, dated `2026-04-09`, contextually mapped with `date_and_update_label_match` confidence to `ea_u1_0.2.0_build_22674441` (Steam build `22674441`; semantic version `0.2.0` is inferred). On the source-snapshot axis, the current immutable snapshot is `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, using SRDB `2.3.4` and captured at `2026-07-11T05:02:30.009644Z`. `ea_u1_0.2.8_build_23761620`—semantic version `0.2.8`, released `2026-06-17`—is only the latest verified public executable observed at capture, not proof that every archived value came from that build. Legacy numeric reports must retain their July 8 boundary and must not receive the canonical snapshot ID unless ported and rerun against that snapshot.

No competing snapshot was installed: the active corpus remains the single canonical RuptureOps snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`. Deduplicated archive material comprises all 468 items, all 191 public buildings, all 234 recipe definitions, 6 corporations and 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 development upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot entries, and the official-news subset; these overlap the richer canonical corpus. The comparison found 467 substantive item matches and corrected two canonical normalization defects: the `airlock` item had been overwritten by a building-shaped detail response, and Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` sentinel was normalized to null. Selectively promoted material was limited to: player save model `rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v.2 associations linking `mechanical-drill-tier2` to impure and pure recipes for Calcium, Titanium, and Wolfram; 15 medium-confidence consumable-effect assumptions retained separately with a warning that they lack per-value URLs and require first-party or in-game verification; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. These curated additions do not overwrite raw source records, while legacy reports and models remain verified raw-import material until recomputed.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family—four named report/source artifacts, `build_flowworks_report.py`, `flowworks_campaign_analysis.py`, and twelve `flowworks_*` CSV outputs—is `superseded_audit_only`: it overemphasized output storage and led to an overbuilt three-Stabilizer/two-slow-press plan. It is retained solely as historical audit evidence and must not become current guidance. Active authority is `Player save - progression and next builds.md`, whose Flowworks plan is explicitly adopted but still `planned_not_installed`: start with 10 machines including 1 Titanium Excavator, 1 Wolfram Excavator, 1 Titanium Smelter, 1 Wolfram Smelter, 1 Titanium Rod v2, 1 Wolfram Powder v2, 1 Wolfram Plate v2, 1 Stabilizer, 1 Impeller, and 1 Turbine; then add 1 Titanium Smelter, Sheet v2, Beam, Housing, 1 Nozzle, and 2 Valves, adding a second v1 Titanium Excavator only if the selected node is Impure; add 2 Pumps for the Pressure Tank research-plus-production pack; add the second Stabilizer only before Scanner/levels 11–12; and build one reserved HRS v2 only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. After that second Stabilizer, planned peak imports are HRS 54/min, Helium-3 72/min, Sulphuric Acid 56/min, Rotor 60/min, and Stator 10/min, total 252/min, fitting one 480/min Rail v3 trunk before buffer smoothing. Current evidence still describes Flowworks as a selected site with no confirmed Core, production placement, or construction.

answer.answer: Landmark-grounded geography checkpoint completed from the frozen corpus only. Grand Basin’s older Red Lake/Redleaf match is superseded; relational pins remain explicitly bounded; screenshot registration is not combined with SRDB coordinates.

claims.value: The earlier provisional Grand Basin match to the Red Lake/Redleaf basin was wrong. The canonical Grand Basin Reserve is the broad basin north of the active production corridor and immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry”; Mythic Cry lies in the mountains immediately west at approximately `2518.767,3099.107`. The basin’s northern/northwestern pad is broad and relatively flat. Grand Basin is selected but not confirmed built, and its map marker denotes the basin area rather than a future Core. The first active campus/Core should remain east of the mountain boundary, with a POI/cliff combat exclusion strip, while the Geo Scanner near `3059,2618` stays outside the first district.
source_paths: corpus/Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Flowworks is a selected, not-confirmed-built Titanium/Wolfram mechanical Works on a broad field between the two active sites Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. Faraday is east/southeast of Flowworks and immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn.” No Flowworks Core or production placement is confirmed. The dashed Landerworks–Flowworks–Faraday axis records this relationship only; it is not surveyed rail geometry.
source_paths: corpus/Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Keep screenshot registration and SRDB coordinates as separate frames unless a transform is verified. SRDB coordinates support proximity searches only inside the captured SRDB map space and must not be combined with screenshots, another map, raw Unreal world coordinates, or route-planner coordinates. The overview’s site pins were registered visually: Landerworks has a directly visible base pin; Flowworks is a proposed footprint rather than a placed Core; Faraday is terrain-registered rather than directly labeled in its crop; and Grand Basin’s marker denotes an area rather than a Core. The dashed site axis is relational rather than surveyed geometry. Sunstone Station and Brimstone Utility have known parent relationships—Sunstone is near/subordinate to Landerworks, and Brimstone feeds Faraday—but neither has an exact registered pin.

The preferred first permanent Goethite satellite is the safer northwestern triple at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`, northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin. It is preferred over the closer western field around `1252–1472,2950–3282` because that field overlaps scanner/hostile envelopes. Build all three Laser Drills on the first permanent visit, merge them into one Goethite-only Cargo Dispatcher, and receive 45 raw Ore/min through one Receiver; a geographically separate fourth drill is only an empty-buffer fallback and requires its own Dispatcher/Receiver pair. The preferred first Oil satellite is approximately `1234,3760`, west/southwest of Mythic Cry and Grand Basin. One Oil Extractor supplies 10 Crude/min through one Crude-only Dispatcher/Receiver pair into one V2 buffer and one GB-A Refinery. A second western marker around `1351,4473` is a separate site, not a same-pad extension; reserve but do not initially build its second pair and Refinery because duplicating extraction also duplicates the expensive Titanium- and Calcium-fed refining line. Ship compact raw Goethite and Crude, then process beside Grand Basin consumers because both resources expand heavily during processing.

answer.answer: The inherited archive requests collapse to one canonical reconciliation keyed by the verified archive identity. No additional promotion is warranted from this frozen corpus. claims.value: Historical topology: `019f4f6d-169c-70e2-8de4-81722b41eee9` began Update 1 research/corpus bootstrap; `019f5263-8bae-7d10-b944-0fd4a543afb9` established the clean RuptureOps bootstrap and repo/vault ownership split; `019f52a5-72aa-7c11-853c-5de258361b42` handled general import/reconciliation; `019f52fa-6195-7701-96a2-da6ec7ef7a08` continued live exploration; `019f52fa-6917-78a3-b1e5-7e631263b4a5` was the logistics fork; `019f52fa-7180-7552-a3b1-09be4c3ee493` was the exploration fork explicitly carrying the same inherited archive-import request; and `019f531d-ba10-7d50-958e-4cffc089c334` handled rupture-cycle product research and an interrupted native build. Forks inheriting `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` are replaying one request, not performing independent imports or adding independent corroboration.

Idempotent archive identity is import ID `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z` plus the immutable `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` identity: 21,674,717 bytes, SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`, 115 manifested files, verified integrity, and archive capture time `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`. Replay rule: when those identifiers match the existing ledger and immutable source copies, reopen the successful reconciliation and its promotion receipts; do not extract a competing import or promote overlapping facts again. The recorded import completed at `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`; its raw tree is intentionally Git-ignored while tracked manifests/checksums provide auditability.

Canonicality rule: the active game-data corpus is only snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`; the imported archive is audit evidence, not a competing snapshot. Its duplicated item, building, recipe, progression, export, map, loot, and official-news material stays unpromoted; only distinct player context, six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer links, explicit consumable assumptions, nine site assets, and consolidated player notes were promoted. Legacy calculations remain under their July 8 boundary until ported and rerun, and the superseded Flowworks study remains raw audit history. Dirty-tree safety is separate but mandatory: the recorded native-app work was on `main`, which already contained unrelated data-pipeline, import, model, and curated-source changes; iOS additions were isolated under untracked `ios/`, and no pre-existing dirty file may be reverted or silently absorbed into an iOS commit. Because the dirty-tree observation is frozen at `2026-07-11 23:14 UTC`, a continuation must inspect live repository truth before changing anything.

Create exactly one continuation checkpoint for all archive-request forks: record the archive reconciliation as verified and complete under import ID `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z`, direct every duplicate fork to reopen that checkpoint, and forbid additional promotion unless genuinely distinct evidence is found and receipted. Keep the separate native-build lane marked historical and incomplete: at the frozen cutoff it lacked an `@main` entry, SwiftUI Mission Timeline view, successful `xcodebuild`, unit/UI-test success, simulator launch or visual/interaction QA, and device-signing/install handoff. The next agent must first inspect live repository state, preserve unrelated dirty work, then finish and verify those acceptance gates; it must not claim the frozen checkpoint is current or install-ready.
